neighbours.label: the word that introduces public reaction to a release or event: 'opened to [acclaim]', 'met with', 'subject of [debate]', 'sparked', 'amid'
fire: The play opened on Broadway in 1964 to rave reviews from nearly every critic.
Her debut novel was met with harsh criticism when it came out last autumn.
The new stadium design has been the subject of fierce argument among local fans.
The proposal to raise bus fares sparked anger among commuters and students.
The game launched in Japan in March to enthusiastic praise from players.
The minister resigned amid growing outrage over the leaked emails.
When the statue was unveiled, it was greeted with jeers from the crowd.
The concert tour began in London to sold-out crowds and glowing press.
quiet: The musical first ran in 1964 at a small theater on 45th Street.
Her debut novel came out last autumn from a small press in Vermont.
The new stadium was designed by an architect from Copenhagen.
The bus company raised fares by ten cents on the first of June.
The game was released in Japan in March for the handheld console.
The minister resigned on Tuesday and moved back to his hometown.
The statue was carved from white marble by a local sculptor.
The concert tour starts in London and ends in Berlin in August.

notes: Probe: premiered to a standing ovation 1.03, sparked protests 0.95, subject of heated debate 0.90, amid controversy 0.87, reopened to praise 0.70, met with mixed reviews 0.63; bridge opened to traffic 0.21; opened in 2001 on a corner 0.05, born in 1950 0.005. It is predictive: it fires on the preposition/verb before the reaction noun.
